title: An exact pruning rule for optimal LZ77-style parsing with k repeat-offset slots
statement: Model: a string s of length n is parsed from position 0 to n by tokens, carrying k slots R = (R[0..k-1]), initially (1, ..., 1): a literal (cost 9); a repeat of slot j with length L >= REPMIN, allowed if R[j] <= i and the text matches at distance R[j] (cost 3 + j + gamma(L); slot j moves to the front); a new match with distance d <= i and length L >= 2 (cost 2 + gamma(L-1) + gamma(d); d is pushed to the front and the last slot dropped); gamma(x) = 2 floor(log2 x) + 1. For slot tuples R != R' let a0 be the first index where they differ and D(R, R') = sum_{a >= a0} max(0, gamma(R[a]) - 1 - a). Theorem 1 (G3): if REPMIN >= 2, every continuation from (i, R) to position n can be simulated from (i, R') at extra cost at most D(R, R'), for arbitrary tuples. Theorem 2: if REPMIN >= 2, the forward DP over (position, slots) that at each position deletes every state R with value >= c(R*) + D(R, R*), for one chosen cheapest state R* (any choice), returns the optimum. Theorem 3 (G3*): the same holds for arbitrary static costs lit, new(L, d), rep(L, j) with the margin sum_{a >= a0} max(0, max_{j >= a, REPMIN <= L <= n - i} [new(L, R[a]) - rep(L, j)]); the maximum over j >= a cannot be replaced by j = a in the continuation bound (counterexample aaaababa). The margin D is attained (V(11,(9,5)) - V(11,(3,5)) = 5 = D on aabbbbabbaabaaaab, k = 2); with REPMIN = 1 the rule fails (aaaaba: optimum 32, G3-pruned DP 33 for k = 1, 2, 3 and every comparator choice); with adaptive costs the one-value-per-state DP fails (bbba); the margins K1 (k = 2, 3), NS (k = 2, 3) and NB, NB0 (k = 2) fail on explicit strings (REPMIN = 2).

bases: Folklore DP over (position, slot contents) and its approximate threshold pruning: Bloom 2015, blog post '01-23-15 - LZA New Optimal Parse' (not peer-reviewed)
provenance.pending_note: The base is the folklore slot-content DP: Bloom's blog posts contain a {Pos,State} parser with a threshold early out (2011) and the DP with the repeat-match offsets in the state, pruned by a threshold he calls approximate (2015), without proof. Beyond the sources read, this note proves the exact pruning rule G3/G3*. Three sources that might contain it could not be read (missing_sources): the journal version of the dictionary-symbolwise flexible parsing (DSFP) paper and the full text of Langiu's Zip-case paper (the publisher's site refused automated access; the DSFP preprint was read in full and has no repeat-offset state), and the 2010 thesis 'Parsing algorithms for data compression' (University of Pisa; not consultable until 2050). Whether they contain the result could not be checked, so it may be our own result. Nothing read states an exact pruning rule of this kind.
